As a Supervisory IT Specialist (INFOSEC), you will perform the following duties: Oversee the procurement, development, integration, modification, operation, maintenance, and disposal of a Federal Information Security Modernization Act (FISMA) system in accordance with National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) 800-12.

Conduct system security evaluation and ensure the rigorous application of information security and information assurance policies, principles, and practices in the delivery of all Information Technology (IT) services.

Conduct risk and vulnerability assessment of planned and installed information systems to identify vulnerabilities, risks, and protection needs. Apply the Risk Management Framework (RMF) as it applies to Federal Information Systems and analyze and determine the Risk Mitigation process.

Perform a full range of supervisory functions, including developing and evaluating performance standards, giving advice, counsel, or instruction to employees. Make or approve selections for subordinate positions and identify training needs.

POSITION REQUIREMENTS: Applicants must possess the following two certifications: A current Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP), also known as (ISC)2, AND a Global Information Assurance Certification (GIAC) Certified Incident Handler (GCIH).

Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP) is an independent information security certification granted by the International Information System Security Certification Consortium, also known as (ISC)2 Global Information Assurance Certification (GIAC) Certified Incident Handler (GCIH) The GIAC Incident Handler certification validates a practitioner's ability to detect, respond, and resolve computer security incidents using a wide range of essential security skills.

GCIH certification holders have the knowledge needed to manage security incidents by understanding common attack techniques, vectors and tools, as well as defend against and respond to such attacks when they occur. Incumbent must have a current or past System Owner designation of a Federal Information Security Modernization Act (FISMA) system.

CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENTS: Ship sailing and aircraft flight time supporting platform IT infrastructure, applications, or sensor instrumentation during mission operations. This position will be filled under the DOC Alternative Personnel System (CAPS). Under CAPS, positions are classified by career, pay plan, and pay band.

In accordance with Office of Personnel Management policy, federal employees are assumed to have gained experience by performing duties and responsibilities appropriate for their official series and grade level as described in their position description.

Experience that would not normally be part of the employee's position is creditable, however, when documented by satisfactory evidence, such as a signed memorandum from the employee's supervisor or an SF-50 or SF-52 documenting an official detail or other official assignment.

Symmetrio is recruiting a Cloud Support Engineer for its customer, a rapidly growing international healthcare SaaS company aggressively expanding in the United states. The Cloud Support Engineer will be a trusted technical face to our customer’s stakeholders: oncology centers, clinics, and health systems.

Collaborating with healthcare IT and clinical application teams across the United States, the Cloud Support Engineer will ensure reliability and provide professional IT support to users of the application.

In this role, you'll provide Tier 1/Tier 2 technical support while serving as a collaborative member of our customer’s engineering team consisting of Site Reliability Engineers and Cloud Network Engineers.

The Cloud Support Engineer will diagnose incidents and cases (SaaS application, AWS cloud infrastructure, customer network connectivity, etc.) and coordinate seamlessly with customer and internal engineering teams to resolve them.

Additionally, the Cloud Support Engineer will develop support playbooks and documentation as the company scales, and help establish best practices for healthcare SaaS support—ideal for someone who combines technical problem-solving, healthcare IT domain expertise, and the professional presence and communication skills required by end users.
This is a full-time, remote position $90,000-$105,000 and a comprehensive benefits package, including health benefits, a 401(k) plan, paid time off, and additional company-sponsored benefits.

Serve as the primary technical contact for assigned customers; represent the company professionally and build trust with customer IT directors, network engineers, and clinical leadership
Provide Tier 1/Tier 2 technical support via phone, email, and ticketing system; triage issues, diagnose root causes, and coordinate resolution with the Principal SRE and Cloud Network Engineers
Troubleshoot application performance issues within the SaaS platform; work with the SRE to identify degradation and escalate appropriately
Diagnose customer connectivity and network issues affecting SaaS platform access, including VPN tunnel health, AWS routing validation, and firewall rule problems; possess working knowledge of Cisco ASA, Fortinet, and Palo Alto firewall environments
Coordinate with customer firewall/network teams during troubleshooting; ask informed questions about firewall rules, NAT settings, and VPN tunnel parameters
Serve as the liaison between customer health system IT departments and internal engineering; gather detailed diagnostic information, validate customer network topology, and communicate complex cloud networking problems clearly
Develop and maintain support playbooks and runbooks focused on cloud networking scenarios specific to healthcare environments: VPN tunnel validation, connectivity health checks, firewall coordination during maintenance windows, and application troubleshooting
Support new customer onboarding; validate initial connectivity, work with customer IT/firewall teams to ensure proper VPN configuration, and coordinate go-live health checks
Proactively monitor customer health indicators (connectivity status, VPN tunnel status, application performance) and alert the SRE/Network Engineer to emerging issues before customers report.
Partner with the Cloud Network Engineer during customer firewall coordination calls; understand oncology center/health system network architectures and validate that connectivity requirements align with customer firewall policies
Build and maintain the support knowledge base with healthcare-specific scenarios; document common oncology center network configurations and troubleshooting patterns
Participate in on-call rotation for critical customer incidents, with escalation support from the SRE and Network Engineer

AWS Certified Advanced Networking – Specialty OR AWS Certified SysOps Administrator – Associate
2+ years of Tier 1/Tier 2 technical support experience in healthcare IT environments (hospitals, clinics, health systems)
Strong familiarity with healthcare network infrastructure and security; comfortable troubleshooting in regulated healthcare environments
Working knowledge of Cisco ASA firewalls; familiarity with Fortinet and Palo Alto environments a plus
Understanding of firewall rule configuration, VPN tunnel setup (Site-to-Site VPN basics), and how healthcare networks connect to external cloud applications
Experience supporting oncology centers, radiation therapy departments, or similar clinical IT environments strongly preferred
Experience supporting Epic EHR, OIS (Oncology Information Systems), or other healthcare applications
Understanding of cloud networking concepts: VPN connectivity, AWS VPCs, firewalls, routing (cloud-based, not traditional BGP/OSPF)
Experience troubleshooting connectivity issues between hospital networks and cloud environments preferred
Strong troubleshooting methodology; ability to think systematically through multi-layer problems (application, cloud infrastructure, customer network)
Excellent communication skills; ability to translate technical concepts for non-technical clinical staff and speak authoritatively with experienced hospital IT directors and network engineers
Professional demeanor and strong customer service orientation
Experience with ticketing systems, knowledge base tools, and technical documentation practices
Comfortable working in a remote environment with self-management and time-zone flexibility for U.S. customer base
Collaborative mindset; comfortable escalating appropriately and partnering with senior engineers
Willingness to develop and own support processes and playbooks in a rapidly growing organization
Given the customer-facing nature of this role, interviews with qualified candidates will be conducted via Microsoft Teams or another video conferencing platform.

Continuously identify and analyze threats and vulnerabilities to the information systems to maintain an appropriate level of protection. Responsible for ensuring the protection of COMSEC materials and to determine and enforce limited access of such materials to proper individuals based on training, clearance and a need to know.

Implement procedures to ensure protection of information transmitted using local or wide area networks, the worldwide web or other communications modes. Implement procedures to ensure the safeguarding and accounting of all COMSEC materials received, distributed, shipped, stored, and destroyed; conducts inventories on all COMSEC.

Report to Major Command (MAJCOM), Air Force Communications Agency (AFCA), National Security Agency (NSA), and Air Force Computer Emergency Response Team (AFCERT) all incidents involving viruses, tampering, or unauthorized system entry.

Provide technical training and instruction on Information Awareness training program procedures to supervisors, employees, and/or unit security representatives.
